estimates.qualifier: 'resulting in 24 fatalities and leaving over 70 persons missing'

fatalities.notes: Two peer-reviewed abstracts disagree (178 vs 24 fatalities plus >70 missing); the range spans both and carries no best

bulked_volume_m3.notes: Sattar et al. (2025): the flood 'eroded ~270 million cubic meters of sediment' and drained '~50 million cubic meters of the lake's water'; Zhang et al. (2025): '38.49 × 10^6 m3 of water was released'. These are flood volumes, not a bulked avalanche volume, so the field stays null.

public_estimates.qualifier: water released at the breach (modelled hydrograph)

dammed_river.notes: Not established in any source retrieved on 2026-09-03; dammed_river was previously recorded as false with that caveat in notes. Null until a fetched source states it either way.

fall_height_m.notes: A lateral-moraine collapse into a lake; the retrieved abstracts state an impact wave height (~20 m, Sattar et al. 2025; overtopping 16.11 m, Zhang et al. 2025), not a fall height.

peak_velocity_ms.notes: Zhang et al. (2025) give an impulse-wave displacement speed of ~26 m/s and a peak discharge of 3.02 × 10^5 m3/s from modelling; no flow velocity of the mass movement was read.

rock_fraction.notes: Moraine (sediment) collapse; not a rock–ice avalanche.

secondary_surge.notes: Not established in any source retrieved on 2026-09-03; secondary_surge was previously recorded as false with that caveat in notes. Null until a fetched source states it either way.

seismic.notes: No seismic record of the moraine collapse was retrieved.

source_elevation_m.notes: The lake/moraine elevation was not read in the retrieved abstracts.

infrastructure_impacts.description: Mohanty et al. (2026): 'destroyed ... a major hydropower plant in the Chungthang region'; Zhang et al. (2025): 'the destruction of three downstream hydropower projects'; Sattar et al. (2025): 'overwhelmed infrastructure, including hydropower installations along the Teesta River'
Mohanty et al. (2026): 'The GLOF also destroyed 13 bridges'

name: South Lhonak Lake moraine collapse and outburst flood, Sikkim, India
notes: Negative control: a moraine-dam / glacial-lake outburst cascade that serac must discriminate from bedrock rock–ice avalanches. dammed_river is false because the flood originated from an existing moraine-dammed lake rather than from a landslide dam; secondary_surge is false because the outburst was the primary flood, not a secondary surge behind a new blockage (both per the retrieved abstracts). Sattar et al. (2025) is a Science paper whose abstract was read via the Europe PMC API.

runout_km.notes: 'The impact of the GLOF extended to 169 km downstream' (Zhang et al. 2025)

source_location.basis: OpenStreetMap Nominatim result for 'South Lhonak' (South Lhonak Glacier, way 134410531); the lateral moraine that collapsed into the proglacial lake adjoins this glacier

estimates.qualifier: '14.7 million cubic meters of frozen lateral moraine collapsing into South Lhonak Lake'
'estimated collapse material volume of 16.75 × 10^6 m3' (lateral moraine)
'a landslide, that dumped a substantial amount (~ 38.31 million m3) of debris into the South Lhonak Lake'
'lost a big chunk of ice mass (~ 7 million m3) due to calving' (glacier, not included in low/high)

source_volume_m3.notes: Three peer-reviewed abstracts give 14.7, 16.75 and 38.31 ×10^6 m3 for the mass entering the lake; no best is chosen

sources.excerpt: triggered by 14.7 million cubic meters of frozen lateral moraine collapsing into South Lhonak Lake. The impact generated an ~20-meter tsunami-like impact wave, which breached the moraine and drained ~50 million cubic meters of the lake's water

sources.title: The Sikkim flood of October 2023: Drivers, causes, and impacts of a multihazard cascade

sources.excerpt: On the night of October 3, 2023, the moraine-dammed South Lhonak Lake in Sikkim suddenly discharged a substantial volume of water, resulting in a glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) that caused 178 fatalities and the destruction of three downstream hydropower projects

time.basis: 'On the night of October 3, 2023' (Zhang et al. 2025); 'On October 4, 2023' local (Mohanty et al. 2026); 'On 3 October 2023' (Sattar et al. 2025). No clock time was read; the instant is 23:30 IST on 3 October with a six-hour uncertainty
